preamble: Loss of the voiceless uvular stop [q] is attested in Oceanic Austronesian. Proto-Oceanic *q, a uvular stop inherited from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *q, disappeared without trace in Fijian and many Southeast Solomonic languages (POc *qupi 'yam' > Fijian uvi, Gela uvi). Polynesian reflexes such as Samoan ufi went through a glottal stop first (PPn *q = [ʔ], kept in Tongan ʻufi). The Arabic qāf > [ʔ] change likewise ends in a glottal stop, not zero. Those cases belong under q_to_glottal_stop.

examples.note: Initial *q lost with no glottal reflex; *p > v.
Also Bughotu and Simbo uvi, Kwaio ufi.

sources: Lynch, J., Ross, M., & Crowley, T. (2002). The Oceanic Languages. Curzon Press.
